text:
Dev Patel: Got a live question from Prospect A (enterprise security review) and need a crisp answer today. They’re asking:
1) “What’s your audit log retention by default and can we configure it (30/90/365/7y)?”
2) “Can we export audit logs to our SIEM and keep them longer there?”
3) “Can you prove enforcement / deletion happens?”

They want something we can put in email + attach whatever ‘compliance report’ we have.

Rachel Kim: Looping in @Markus Klein @Kevin Osei @Naomi Feldman @Olga Petrov — this is the exact thing they’ve been pushing on. Also: they asked whether exports include retention boundary info (time range, generated at) and whether we can do “never delete” for audit logs.

Markus Klein: For talk track / email-safe language, use the enablement FAQ here (internal): sources/confluence/sales-enablement/security-faq/retention-controls-and-compliance-reporting-faq.json

Relevant bullets:
- Audit logs default: 365 days (Hosted), configurable with guardrails 30–2555 days (~7 years)
- Retention applies to Redwood-managed storage; customer can export to SIEM/archive and keep longer under their own retention
- We don’t promise “instant deletion at exactly expiry” — it’s TTL/scheduled jobs with bounded delay + monitoring

Kevin Osei: +1. On exports specifically:
- We can say we support audit log exports in download-friendly format (JSONL/CSV depending on workflow) and customers can automate ingestion to SIEM.
- Retention affects what remains queryable/exportable from Redwood. We can’t retroactively export events that already aged out.
- Export payload includes metadata about the export (generation timestamp, requested range). We also warn if requested range predates retention window.

Naomi Feldman: On “never delete” — don’t say yes. We have guardrails and “never delete” is not allowed by default. If they need longer than max, position export to customer-managed archive. For true holds: legal hold exists but it’s restricted and requires approval.

Dev Patel: Helpful. They asked if legal hold can be customer-operated in Hosted.

Naomi Feldman: For Hosted/Dedicated, legal hold is typically managed through Redwood support engagement (RBAC + approvals) to avoid mis-scoping. For Private it can be customer-operated depending on admin model. Phrase it as “supported; scoped and auditable; operational model depends on deployment.”

Olga Petrov: For “prove enforcement,” we should offer evidence types, not internals. Approved external artifacts:
- Compliance Reporting Pack (v1) under NDA (control-to-evidence matrix + retention narrative)
- Redacted screenshots of Console showing effective policy and enforcement status (last run)
- Redacted sample audit events demonstrating retention policy changes are audited

Do NOT send internal dashboards/runbooks.

Markus Klein: If they want an attachment: the current customer-shareable bundle is the Compliance Reporting Pack (v1) draft. Use the standard pack; don’t customize in-line. If you need the latest PDF/ZIP, ping me and I’ll pull the latest build.

Rachel Kim: Can we provide a one-paragraph answer for the email?

Kevin Osei: Draft email language (feel free to tighten):
“Redwood supports tenant-configurable retention for audit logs. Audit logs are retained by default for 365 days (Hosted) and can be configured within guardrails (e.g., 30 days up to ~7 years). Retention is enforced via automated TTL/deletion mechanisms (implementation varies by datastore) and is monitored and auditable. Retention applies to Redwood-managed storage; customers can export audit logs for SIEM ingestion/archival and retain exported logs under their own policies. Export workflows include metadata (generation time and time range) to make boundaries clear.”

Naomi Feldman: Add one sentence: “We do not offer ‘never delete’ by default; longer-term retention is typically met via export to customer-managed archive, and legal hold is supported with appropriate approvals.”

Dev Patel: Great. What about their request: “We want 90 days retention for *all logs* (infra logs too).”

Markus Klein: Be precise: v1 is not “all logs.” We should say: retention controls cover audit logs + selected operational/analytics datasets. Some infra/vendor logs are governed by provider constraints and SRE standards and are not customer-configurable in v1. (This is explicitly in the FAQ.)

Olga Petrov: If they ask for contractual commitments about infra logs, route to Security & Compliance + legal. Don’t over-commit in a support email.

Rachel Kim: Also they’re asking “can you show us where in the product we set this?”

Kevin Osei: You can say: “Console → Security & Compliance → Data Retention” shows effective policy + enforcement status. We can provide redacted screenshots as part of the reporting pack.

Dev Patel: Perfect. I’ll reply to the prospect with the paragraph + offer the Compliance Reporting Pack (v1) under NDA and mention we can provide redacted screenshots/evidence. @Markus Klein can you send me the latest pack link/attachment?

Markus Klein: Yep, will DM you the current PDF/ZIP. (Reminder: share externally under NDA only; standard distribution per internal process.)

Naomi Feldman: :thumbsup: If they push on “instant deletion” or “never delete,” loop me in before replying.

Dev Patel: Thanks all — sending response now.
